Scope: implement backend changes for the update (partial-update) API for the resource that has a description field. Only the update endpoint(s) accept the new control field clear_description; do not change behavior of create or read endpoints except to document that responses must not include clear_description.

Rules to implement (explicit, canonical):
1) New request field: clear_description (optional boolean). Default semantics: absent or false = no special action. The presence of clear_description in requests is only supported on update endpoints.

2) Validation rules (all result in HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity):
   - If the request payload includes description with the JSON value null => return 422. (description=null is forbidden.)
   - If clear_description == true and the request payload includes the description field (regardless of the description value, including empty string) => return 422. (clear_description=true is mutually exclusive with supplying description in the same request.)

3) Update semantics (atomic within the request):
   - If clear_description == true and description is not present in payload => set the stored description to the empty string "".
   - If clear_description is absent or false:
       * If description is not present in payload => do not modify the stored description (leave as-is).
       * If description is present and not null => set the stored description to the provided string value (the empty string "" is an allowed explicit value and should be persisted as such).

4) Response and API surface constraints:
   - The update response MUST NOT include clear_description in the response body. Remove/ignore it in serializers/responses.
   - The API must continue returning description in responses per existing behavior.
   - Only update endpoints accept clear_description. Create endpoints MUST NOT accept clear_description (validate and reject if present on create if your API previously forbids unknown fields). If your API tolerates unknown fields on create, document that clear_description is ignored on create.

5) Request parsing & schema changes:
   - Update the update (PATCH/PUT partial) request JSON schema/OpenAPI spec as follows:
       * description: string (nullable=false). Do not allow null. Optional for PATCH.
       * clear_description: boolean, optional. Default behavior: treated as false when absent. Do not set a server-side default value into the DB unless semantics above require it.
   - Add schema-level constraint (or enforce in validation code): If clear_description == true then description must be absent.

6) Implementation checklist (server-side code path):
   - Parse JSON body and detect presence vs absence of keys. You must distinguish between absent and present-with-value (especially for description and clear_description).
   - Validate request: return 422 with a JSON error body if any validation rule from (2) fails. Error responses should identify the offending field(s) and reason (e.g. "description must not be null", "clear_description cannot be provided together with description").
   - Within the update transaction:
       * Determine whether description should be updated using rules in (3).
       * Apply only the determined changes to the persisted record. Do not modify description when both clear_description absent/false and description absent.
   - Commit transaction and serialize response WITHOUT the clear_description field.

7) Concurrency and atomicity:
   - Apply update to description in the same DB update operation used for other fields to avoid race conditions (single SQL UPDATE or single ORM save in the update transaction).
   - If using optimistic locking or ETag versioning, ensure the change to description participates in the same version check as other changed fields.

8) Tests to add (automated unit and integration tests):
   - Update with {clear_description:true} (and no description key) => 200/204 as existing update semantics; DB description becomes ""; response contains no clear_description.
   - Update with {clear_description:true, description:""} => 422.
   - Update with {clear_description:true, description:"something"} => 422.
   - Update with {description:null} => 422.
   - Update with {description:""} and no clear_description => description becomes "" (explicit allowed).
   - Update with neither clear_description nor description => description preserved (no change).
   - Update with clear_description false and no description => no change to description.
   - Ensure create endpoint behavior unchanged; test that clear_description is not accepted on create (or is ignored per your API contract) and that description=null remains rejected on create if previously rejected.
   - Test response bodies do not include clear_description fields under any circumstance.

9) Documentation / OpenAPI / changelog:
   - Update the OpenAPI spec for the update endpoint: add clear_description (boolean, optional) to request body schema, add note that clear_description must not be present together with description; description is not nullable; state that clear_description will not appear in responses.
   - Document the front-end clearing contract explicitly: front-end must clear description by sending {"clear_description": true} and must not send description simultaneously.

10) Error messages and status codes:
   - Use HTTP 422 for validation failures described in (2).
   - Error response bodies should be consistent with existing API error format and list field-specific errors for description and clear_description.

11) Backward compatibility and defaults:
   - Because clear_description is optional and defaults to no-op when absent or false, existing clients remain compatible.
   - Do not add any default mutation when clear_description is absent or false; absence implies no change unless description is supplied.

12) Logging and metrics:
   - Optionally log validation failures for monitoring with the reason (e.g., invalid null description, conflicting fields).

13) Implementation notes per common stacks:
   - When using frameworks that coerce missing fields to null (e.g., form parsers), ensure request-parsing preserves presence/absence (use raw JSON body parsing and check key existence rather than relying on bound object fields that default to null). Failure to preserve presence will make it impossible to distinguish "absent" vs "present with null".
   - If your serializer automatically drops unknown fields from output, ensure clear_description is not added there; explicitly exclude it from output models if needed.

Acceptance criteria (explicit):
   - All validation rules from (2) enforced and tested.
   - Update semantics from (3) implemented.
   - clear_description is only accepted on update and is never returned in responses.
   - description=null requests return 422; description empty string is accepted and persisted.
   - Front-end clearing by submitting {"clear_description":true} clears description to "" and is accepted by the update endpoint.

Do not implement any behavior not listed above. Do not change other API fields or response formats except to ensure clear_description is not returned. Ensure tests and OpenAPI docs reflect these constraints.
